basis: Generalized epidermal peeling defines both subtypes; atopy in the inflammatory subtype does not establish immune disease across the umbrella.
Disordered skeletal-muscle excitability defines the group; neurologic and cardiac involvement are subtype-dependent.
Spirometra larval infection; subcutaneous invasion with inflammatory nodules occurs in over 30%; ocular and cerebral disease vary geographically.
Highly heterogeneous umbrella; neurodevelopmental impairment is common in symptomatic chromosome 2 imbalances, but no additional organ is established across the group.
Vertebral and metaphyseal dysplasia occurred in 4/4 patients; cardiac, vascular and developmental findings lack sufficient frequency evidence.
Glycosylation disorder with developmental impairment and intrinsic antibody deficiency; coagulation abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Four-axis cap reached.
Congenital extra digits on the postaxial side; the concept is explicitly nonsyndromic.
Persistent nasal dysfunction following turbinate reduction; nose and nasal airways belong to pulmonary. Cognitive and psychiatric symptoms do not establish brain damage.
Neurodegenerative movement and cognitive disorder; chorea, rigidity, ataxia and cognitive impairment each occur in 30-79%.
Somatoform psychiatric disorder without a specified directly damaged organ.
Anaplasma directly infects neutrophils and causes cytopenias; transient aminotransferase elevation does not establish lasting hepatic damage.
ID and hypogonadism 80-99%; skeletal abnormalities/low bone density and severe sensorineural hearing loss 80-99%. Ocular anomalies omitted at the four-axis cap.
Variable intellectual disability is the named neurologic component; congenital abnormalities affect different organs across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Benign tumour arising in the oral cavity; mouth and palate belong to gastrointestinal.
Hypogonadism and developmental impairment 80-99%; skeletal defects and intrinsic dental abnormalities 30-79%. Ocular findings omitted at cap; asthma/otitis are separate diseases.
Acute myeloid neoplasm of marrow and blood; the translocation does not establish common damage to another organ.
Invasive extraintestinal Salmonella infection; respiratory signs alone do not establish common lung damage. Abscesses and meningitis are occasional.
Collecting-duct cysts and congenital hepatic fibrosis define the disease; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Hypertension and hypersplenism are secondary effects.
Inherited lipid-digestion defect with exocrine pancreatic insufficiency and malabsorption in 80-99%; nutritional anemia is secondary, without established direct blood damage.
Brain malformations, oral/intestinal anomalies and cardiac defects define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Short palpebral fissures alone do not establish eye damage.
Isolated developmental eye malformation; microphthalmia documented in 2/3 patients.
EBV-associated mesenchymal neoplasia; tumour sites vary. Smooth-muscle lineage alone does not establish skeletal-muscle involvement.
Developmental malformations of cerebral cortex and other brain structures define the umbrella; ocular abnormalities occur only in selected subtypes.
Tumour occupies the cerebellopontine angle; direct vestibulocochlear nerve injury causes hearing loss in a majority, particularly with vestibular schwannoma.
B-lymphoblast neoplasm of blood/marrow with a lymphoma designation; lymphoma adds the immune mechanism axis. No common additional organ damage is established.
